info.description: The Future AGI platform operations admitted to this SDK release.This is a scoped public copy of the platform's customer contract; openapi/platform/source.json names the source and its sha256. Responses are forward compatible: unknown fields and enum values from a newer server are kept, never rejected.

delete.description: Purges this run's body through the durable tombstone: the messages, steps, approvals, and ratings are removed and the fact of the deletion survives in the conversation log. Ownership is resolved with the same gate GET uses, so an unknown run and another tenant's run both return 404 — deletion cannot be used to discover that someone else's run exists. A run that is still executing is refused with 409; cancel it first. The response states what the deletion did NOT reach.

get.summary: Stream a run's steps, tool calls, and output as server-sent events
get.description: Streams the strict omega-workspace/v1 event union. Resume strictly after the last durable sequence with Last-Event-ID (preferred) or the after query fallback. Last-Event-ID takes precedence when both are present. Ephemeral message_delta and activity_output frames do not advance the durable resume cursor; a reconnect can therefore begin with a cumulative in-progress snapshot that replaces the client's ephemeral overlay.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Preferred canonical non-negative durable event sequence to resume strictly after.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Query fallback used only when Last-Event-ID is absent.

parameters.name: transport
parameters.description: Absent: the stream as always. `stream`: the same stream, opened at once by an SSE comment and kept alive by one every 15 s. `poll`: one long-poll window for a client behind a buffering proxy; the response ends once it carried frames, or empty at `wait`; resume with Last-Event-ID.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: With transport=poll: how long an empty window stays open, in milliseconds (default and maximum 25000).

200.description: The run's events as Server-Sent Events.

get.summary: Get the per-run step-by-step observation trace for a workspace run
get.description: Returns this run's own attributed, redacted, bounded runtime observations — the step-by-step trace of what its agents actually did — read from the daemon's durable observation log and ordered by the causal (task turn order, seq) order. The same ownership gate as the tree read applies: unknown and cross-tenant conversations both return 404, and a taskId filter naming a task this run does not own answers the same 404 (foreign task ids are never confirmed to exist). The envelope never claims completeness: its window block states exactly what the bounded read examined, and a gap in seq inside one drive means the runtime's own per-drive cap dropped events there — stated in-band — never that this surface lost one.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Restrict the trace to ONE of this conversation's own task ids. A task id this run does not own answers 404, exactly like an unknown conversation.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Exact observation kind filter (e.g. `tool.started`). Must be non-empty when present.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum observations returned (default 500). The oldest are dropped first and the envelope says so via `truncated`. Above 2000 is a 400, never a silent clamp.

post.summary: Send the next turn in a conversation
post.description: Starts a NEW turn; it does not inject guidance into a turn that is already running. A message sent while another turn is still driving is ACCEPTED and durably parked as a queued follow-up (202 with queued=true and the committed user message) instead of being dispatched onto the shared agent process, because concurrent drives corrupted the answer. The parked message dispatches automatically as the next turn — same conversation, bound agent, and history — when the driving turn's task settles, and it survives a server restart. One queued follow-up per conversation: a second message while one is parked is refused with 409 follow_up_queued naming the parked queuedMessageId. A message to a PAUSED run is still refused with 409 run_paused. Requires a durable retry key. Exact same-key retries return the original committed user message with duplicate=true (queued=true while it is still parked); reusing a key with different input or ordered attachment ids returns 409, including after restart.

202.description: New guidance durably committed (duplicate=false); queued=true when it parked behind a driving turn

post.summary: Interrupt a conversation's own run without destroying it
post.description: The NON-DESTRUCTIVE stop. Preempts the in-flight drive of the tasks this conversation owns instead of cancelling them, so the run stays re-drivable and its sandbox, transcript checkpoint and tool journal survive for `POST .../continue` to resume from. Task-scoped, unlike `POST .../pause`, which forwards to the shared bound process. Authorization is `cancel`'s, unchanged: a caller who cannot cancel this run cannot interrupt it. A conversation with nothing in flight is accepted and books no pause marker — a marker with no re-drivable task behind it would render a Continue that could only restart.

post.summary: Continue a conversation's interrupted run
post.description: Re-drives the parked task so completed work is KEPT rather than repeated: committed model turns are threaded back from the transcript checkpoint, and a tool call the model re-requests from the interrupted turn is replayed from the tool journal instead of re-fired. It never falls back to re-submitting the goal — a conversation with no re-drivable parked task is refused 409 `not_resumable` rather than silently starting the work over. The drive is detached: the conversation comes back immediately and progress is observed on `GET .../events`.

get.summary: List the approvals awaiting the caller, or (state=decided) the ones already decided
get.description: Every approval suspended on the caller's own runs, oldest first, assembled from the managed task store rather than from a conversation projection — so it lists approvals the single-valued pendingApproval field cannot carry (a conversation may hold two suspended tasks at once). Scoped by the same ownership predicate the decision route uses: an approval absent here is refused by POST /workspace/approvals/{approvalId}, and one listed here is decidable. conversationId narrows it to one run and is owner-gated exactly like the detail route, so an unknown run and another tenant's run are the same 404.

parameters.description: pending (the default) lists what waits on the caller, oldest first; decided lists what was already approved or denied on the caller's runs, newest first, with who decided (for this reader) and the reason given. Same ownership predicate either way.

alertsDeferred.description: Future AGI made the project but its plan had no room for the two default alerts yet (reason: Future AGI's code for why); null otherwise.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key

FiKeyPair.name: X-Api-Key
FiKeyPair.description: The public half of a Future AGI API key pair (env FI_API_KEY). Always sent with FiKeyPairSecret.

FiKeyPairSecret.name: X-Secret-Key
FiKeyPairSecret.description: The secret half of the key pair (env FI_SECRET_KEY). Never logged, never in a query string.

OmegaBearer.description: Self-host and local: an Omega EE account key (env FUTUREAGI_OMEGA_API_KEY).
